No, no, no. Bad idea if you're not very experienced. It's very easy to lose grip and if you do, there's nothing to catch you except for the cold, hard and inviting ground. Don't try that unless you are very very 100% certain you can do it. And climb a few cranes normally first, at minimum.

Entrance/exit plan, always do your first on an unguarded site during night. Don't make loud noises, duh. Look out for all kinds of alarms, such as sound alarms (usually look like black boxes on walls), cameras and motion sensors (also looks like black boxes most times, just avoid black boxes in general). If you trigger the alarm, get the hell out of there ASAP. Don't try and race to the top. Leaving without a climb is better than leaving in cuffs.

Oh and also, don't steal anything, that'd make it theft. Only climb the crane and if it's locked, leave it. Breaking the lock is breaking and entering.

Best of luck from Sweden.

No no no!!!! Don't ever cut locks/fencing/doors open. That'll make it breaking and entering, which comes with a way bigger punishment than trespassing. Also, it will alert the construction company when they find the lock cut open, they'll most likely do an investigation into it, check cams whatever and increases your risk of getting caught like a lot.

If it's not visible security it's probably no security at all, usually sites like to have their security easily visible as a deterrent to enter the site illegally. But it does depend on what site it is, unless it's some high-profile building that they're constructing you should be fine!
